evals.name: bootstrap-invoicing
evals.prompt: I want to start a new project: a small invoicing service for freelancers (create clients, create and send invoices with VAT, mark them paid, monthly summary). Backend in Python. Please get the project set up properly with documents and architecture guidance. I don't want any application code yet.
evals.expected_output: A project with the five-document set (functional spec, business rules with IDs and codes, use cases referencing IDs, domain model with glossary and ports, technical spec with Python stack and architecture check) plus CLAUDE.md, open points for unknowns, and no application code.
assertions: Business rules are in a table where each rule has an ID like XX-01
Rules that can fail carry an English error code
Every use case lists the rule IDs it applies and check_traceability.py reports no undefined IDs
Functional spec, domain model, technical spec and CLAUDE.md all exist (business rules and use cases may be merged)
No application source code was written beyond folder placeholders and configuration
CLAUDE.md contains the branch rule, the ask-before-adding-dependency rule, test-first for domain code, and pointers to the documents
Technical spec names pytest and an architecture check such as import-linter and a domain/application/adapters layout

Facts the user did not give (VAT rates, currencies, numbering) are recorded as open points or as questions, not silently invented, and no rule fixes a jurisdiction-dependent detail (country, VAT rates, VAT-number format, retention period) while jurisdiction is still open
No rule is restated in another document, verbatim or reworded; other documents cite its ID
Domain model has a ubiquitous language table and a ports table
The branch guard hook is installed in .claude/ and refuses a commit on main

evals.name: build-book-room
evals.prompt: In this project, implement UC-01 Book a room, following the project's documents.
evals.expected_output: Domain and application code for UC-01 with unit tests citing RM-01 and BK-01 to BK-05, a BookingRepository port with an in-memory fake, a PostgreSQL repository with integration tests, no framework imports in the domain, no HTTP route (the technical spec defines none), work not committed on main, and an end-of-task report.
assertions: Work is not done on main without a branch: a feature branch exists or a branch name was proposed, and nothing was committed
Unit tests exist for RM-01, BK-01, BK-02, BK-03, BK-04 and BK-05 and each test names its rule with an @rule tag
Unit tests for domain and service code were created before that code (log order or file times); adapters may get their integration tests after them, as the skill allows
The unit tests pass when run
The domain package imports no web framework or database driver
A BookingRepository port is defined in the application layer and unit tests use an in-memory fake
A test covers the boundary where one booking ends exactly when another starts
A test covers a booking of exactly 8 hours being allowed (BK-04 boundary)
The final report lists rule IDs touched, the test for each, check results and gaps
The report states honestly which checks were run and which were not (integration tests, mypy, import-linter)
No HTTP route or web framework was added, since the technical spec defines no driving adapter for milestone 1
No dependency outside the technical spec stack was added without a recorded question

Documents were changed only in the ways the skill allows without asking (an open point, an approved stack row, folder layout or enforcement table matching new code, the progress plan); any other change has a recorded question
The domain layer calls no platform clock or randomness (datetime.now, uuid4, random); IDs and time come through ports or parameters
A test shows that two overlapping bookings made at the same moment cannot both be stored in PostgreSQL: concurrent requests, or a stale read that only the database constraint catches
Every test tagged with a rule ID exercises that rule's behaviour; a test that covers only part of a rule (such as the count a limit relies on) says so in its tag
No UC-02 (cancel) behaviour was implemented
docs/plan.md was created from the documents, with UC-01 ticked and UC-02 unticked under milestone 1
The run kept a session task list with the mode's steps

evals.name: review-returns-docs
evals.prompt: Our returns desk docs have grown over time and I think they're out of sync. Review them and tell me what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: A report that finds the planted problems, groups them as contradictions, gaps and duplication, runs or mirrors the traceability check, and asks the user to decide instead of silently rewriting rules.
assertions: Finds the 14-day versus 30-day return window contradiction
Finds that UC-02 references an undefined rule RT-09
Finds that RT-06 (audit log) is not referenced by any use case or other document
Finds that the technical spec restates the text of RT-02 and RT-03
Finds that the technical route lets Customers decide returns while RT-04 says only staff
Finds the gift cards contradiction between behaviour and scope
Notes that only RT-02 has a test
Used the traceability script or an equivalent check of IDs

Did not change the meaning of a rule, rule reference or check without asking: only edits with one possible reading (a pointer replacing a copy that says the same thing, a route role aligned with RT-04) are applied directly; everything else is asked as a question with a recommendation
Findings are grouped as contradictions, gaps and duplication or stale text
The RefundCalculator text is reported as a contradiction about where RT-03 is checked, not only as duplication
Work happened on a branch and nothing was committed on main

evals.name: change-booking-limits
evals.prompt: The requirements changed: a member can now hold at most 2 upcoming bookings (it was 3), and a single booking can last at most 4 hours (it was 8). Please update the requirements and the code.
evals.expected_output: Rules BK-01 and BK-04 tightened with the same IDs, no old values left anywhere, tests moved to the new boundaries, a question about existing bookings, and a change report.
assertions: Both rules keep their IDs and the old numbers are gone from documents and code, with no history note; only tests that model previously stored bookings may still use them
Tests are moved to the new boundaries with @rule tags and pass
The limit values live in one place each in the domain or application
The effect on existing bookings is raised as a question with a recommendation
Integration tests were run against the real database
A change report in the skill's format was given
A stored booking longer than the new limit still loads and still blocks its room under BK-02, and a test shows it
The change and its reason are recorded in the technical spec's Decisions
The traceability check was run with the ID-stability comparison against the last commit

evals.name: change-new-use-case
evals.prompt: Members want to see their upcoming bookings. Add that to the project.
evals.expected_output: The change kinds are named, new rules with IDs are added, UC-03 is added without renumbering, documents are updated in order, tests come first, and the report follows the skill's format.
assertions: The kinds of change (use case, and rules if any) are named before editing
New behaviour is stated as rules with IDs in the rules file, not only in the use case
UC-03 is added and existing use case numbers are unchanged
Domain model, technical spec and functional spec are updated by reference to the rule IDs
New tests carry @rule or @usecase tags and were written before the code
No behaviour is invented without being recorded as a question or open point
Every test tagged with a rule ID exercises that rule's behaviour, not only a related query or a part of the rule

evals.name: change-db-swap
evals.prompt: We want to move the persistence adapter from PostgreSQL to MySQL 8.
evals.expected_output: Change confined to the persistence adapter, the new dependency approved, the PostgreSQL-specific overlap guarantee for BK-02 replaced and tested, a Decisions entry written, migrations handled with the user's confirmation, and verified on a real MySQL 8.
assertions: Domain and application layers are unchanged
The new driver is recorded as a question and added to the stack table
The BK-02 guarantee that relied on a PostgreSQL constraint is replaced and covered by a concurrency test
A Decisions entry records what, why and what was rejected
The existing migration is not rewritten without asking whether a real environment applied it
Tests pass against a real MySQL 8 container
The BK-02 guarantee covers every write path, including an update that reactivates a cancelled booking, and a test shows it
Any claim that MySQL cannot support an approach is backed by a minimal test or documentation cited in the Decisions entry
The concurrency test makes both transactions check for overlaps before either inserts, so it fails if any one lock is removed

evals.name: adopt-library-loans
evals.prompt: This repo is the lending desk app for our town library (Flask + PostgreSQL, about three years old). There are no docs and the person who wrote most of it has left, so nobody is sure what all the rules are. We'd like to move it to DDD and hexagonal architecture over time using the ddd-hexagonal workflow. Can you get it started? Lending is what we care about most.
evals.expected_output: Adopt mode on the loans area only: an area map in docs/adoption.md, loan rules found in the code and the schema confirmed into business-rules.md with IDs, use cases with their current Home, the conflicting loan limits and float money raised as findings, the existing tests tagged, characterization tests for the rest on the real database, the architecture check with a baseline of today's violations, no production code changed and the already failing test neither fixed nor deleted, and an adoption report.
assertions: No file under src/ or migrations/ was changed
Work is on a new branch and nothing was committed
The starting state of the test suite is recorded, including test_fee_is_capped failing, and that test is neither fixed, deleted nor skipped
docs/adoption.md maps loans, members and catalog (or equivalent areas), with loans adopted and the other areas not adopted
business-rules.md holds the loan rules with IDs, and no rule of the members or catalog areas (email format, ISBN format, payments) was added
The two rules that exist only in the schema, one open loan per book and at most 2 renewals, are recorded as loan rules
The conflicting loan limits (3 in loans.py, 5 in web.py) are raised as a finding or a question, not resolved silently
Late fees computed on floats are reported as a finding
Each loan rule names where it is enforced today, as file:line evidence in adoption.md or in the technical spec's enforcement table
Existing tests that cover a rule are tagged with its rule ID rather than duplicated
Every loan rule has a test citing its ID or is listed as not testable without changing code, and the traceability check reports no undefined IDs
Tests other than test_fee_is_capped pass, including new tests against the real PostgreSQL database (expected failures allowed)
An architecture check is configured and passes, with today's violations recorded as a baseline instead of fixed or switched off
Adding a new dev tool (such as import-linter) was raised as a question before it was added
There is one recap, right before the first confirmation question, and its top decisions are written as choices
Settled candidates are confirmed in one batch and the decision questions are grouped by concept
For the rules only the database enforces, the user is asked whether the domain should enforce them too
An adoption report in the skill's format opens the final message

evals.name: adopt-confirmation
evals.prompt: This repo is the lending desk app for our town library (Flask + PostgreSQL, about three years old). There are no docs and the person who wrote most of it has left, so nobody is sure what all the rules are. We'd like to move it to DDD and hexagonal architecture over time using the ddd-hexagonal workflow. Can you get it started? Lending is what we care about most.
evals.expected_output: Short run of adopt-library-loans that stops once the confirmation questions for the first area are written: one recap right before them, top decisions written as choices, settled candidates in one batch, decisions grouped by concept, a domain-enforcement question for the database-only rules, and no change to production code.
assertions: No file under src/ or migrations/ was changed
There is one recap, right before the first confirmation question, and its top decisions are written as choices
Settled candidates are confirmed in one batch and the decision questions are grouped by concept
For the rules only the database enforces, the user is asked whether the domain should enforce them too
evals.run_note: Shortened run: stop once the confirmation questions for the first area are in outputs/questions.md (see README, 'Short runs').

evals.name: fix-double-return
evals.prompt: The front desk says a member was charged the late fee twice for the same book: the return got scanned twice by mistake. Can you sort it out?
evals.expected_output: Fix mode on LN-12: the Adopt expected-failure test becomes the reproduction (marker removed, watched failing), a question about members already charged twice with a query and a recommendation and no data changed, the smallest change in loans.py (and the route's error handling), LN-12's text unchanged, the open point closed and the enforcement line updated, all checks green except the pre-existing test_fee_is_capped, and a fix report.
assertions: Work is on a new branch and nothing was committed
The work is treated as a fix of LN-12, and LN-12's rule text in business-rules.md is unchanged
The expected-failure marker on test_returned_loan_cannot_be_returned_again is removed and no second test for the same case is added
The test was seen failing before the code was changed
Members already charged twice are raised as a question with a recommendation and a query that finds them, and no stored data or migration was changed
Only loans.py and web.py changed under src/, with no module moved, renamed or added
Tests other than test_fee_is_capped pass against the real PostgreSQL database, and test_fee_is_capped is unchanged
The LN-12 open point is closed and the enforcement table names where LN-12 is now enforced
Document lines the fix added or changed cite the code it changed by path::symbol, with no line numbers, and the LN-12 enforcement row names the function
The architecture check and the traceability check pass
A fix report in the skill's format opens the final message
In docs/plan.md the LN-12 fix is ticked with a date, "Now" is clear, and the report's follow-ups are added
The run kept a session task list with the mode's steps
